prompts.connect_directive: Before you do anything else, read every resource linked below, whole: they hold the rules you work by and what your task is.
prompts.connect_rules:
Understand the goal through the project before acting. Use project evidence and the assigned task and skills to resolve consequential unknowns. Decide engineering questions from the assignment, the specification and the project's functional map. Record decisions when the assignment calls for it. Ask the user about decisions that require their input. Use the simplest adequate approach. Keep changes relevant to the assignment. Establish the requested outcome and the evidence that will show it. You are expected to follow the specification closely. The designers recognize that a specification can occasionally be short-sighted or ill-conceived. The following mitigation is available for those cases. Do not proceed with a short-sighted specification that introduces aspects which block or hinder the functionality represented by the project's functional map when a better solution is well reasoned and does not introduce issues for other parts of the system. The functionality shown by the project map is the prevailing design. Before adapting the specification, explain what it overlooked or hindered, the affected functional relationships, dependencies and interactions, and how the better solution lets that functionality work properly and perform well without introducing issues elsewhere in the system. In adaptive mode, proceed with the adapted specification only after reasoning from the map and full system design establishes those conditions. Record the adapted specification and surface the change and its reasoning as a message to the user. These messages provide visibility, not approval gates. In strict mode, return the reasoned adaptation as a recommendation without changing the operative specification; do not continue affected work under a specification established to block or hinder the represented functionality. New user instructions revise operative requirements in either mode.
Record intended functionality and its purpose while planning or assigning it, with its source and unresolved details, so later agents can discover that intent. A command's usage instructions are in its help: metaform help <module> <verb>.
Communicate clearly and concisely in grammatical language. Give the outcome, evidence, consequential decisions and remaining work in the detail the recipient needs. Use canonical project terms with their established meanings. Preserve exact identifiers, values, code, error messages and operative source wording. Keep the user's source instructions and revisions distinguishable from interpretation, research and proposals. A navigation summary does not replace its source. Store the substantive result once in its work record and refer to it when coordinating.

prompts.a2a_card: Metaform holds the functional map of a project and puts agents to work on it. Send work as a message: it becomes a ticket at the Address of the element it concerns, worked by an agent with what the map knows there. Name that Address as the contextId under the Address extension; without one, Metaform answers with the Addresses that fit and you reply with one.
prompts.a2a_skill: Opens a ticket at an Address of the project's map; the message's text is the task, and an agent reads the map there, plans its steps, makes the change and records what it learned. The task is submitted while the ticket waits and working while an agent has it, also while it waits on Metaform's person, which metadata waitingOn says; it ends completed with the resolution as an artifact, canceled or failed. It is input-required only when Metaform asks you which Address the work concerns. Send with returnImmediately and follow the task with SubscribeToTask or a push notification: a ticket can take hours, so a send that waits returns after at most seconds.
prompts.a2a_skill_example: Make the kitchen timer's alarm louder: the cook misses it over the extractor fan.
prompts.a2a_extension: With this extension a message's contextId is an Address in the project's map, such as code.manager.route, and the ticket opens there; the map must hold it. Metadata under this extension's URI may give the ticket's title, its kind (broken, flawed or enhancement), and, replying to a task that asks for an Address, the address chosen.

prompts.catalog_tool: Discover commands by their owning module. Read metaform://modules for module descriptions and metaform://<module>/tools for its commands. With module, load only that module. With search, find commands by name or purpose, including misspellings; module optionally narrows the search. With tool and arguments, run the exact command.
prompts.catalog_tool_unkeyed: Discover commands through metaform://modules and metaform://<module>/tools. With module, read that module's commands; with search, find commands by name or purpose, including misspellings. With tool and arguments, run a command. This connection lists discovery alone; use the returned session handle to retain delivery receipts.
prompts.catalog_search: Command names or words describing the desired capability; matching tolerates misspellings.
prompts.catalog_run: A tool to run, by name, with arguments.
prompts.catalog_arguments: The arguments of the tool named in tool.

prompts.connect_catalog: Metaform's commands run in your shell: metaform <module> <verb> <argument>=<value>. Where an instruction names a command as <module>_<verb>, such as map_work, run metaform map work. metaform help <module> lists a module's commands, and metaform help <module> <verb> gives one command's arguments and how to use it. The project's map is read and written with the project tool.
prompts.connect_compaction: When this context is compacted and no runner reports it, call metaform_catalog with compacted=true. Relevant instructions and node context become eligible again when needed. Catalog discovery can remain available; Metaform cannot establish what you retained.
prompts.connect_unkeyed: This connection names no session. Keep the session handle returned by discovery or an instruction prerequisite and pass it as on subsequent calls so instruction receipts stay in the same logical context.

prompts.catalog_none: No command fits those words. Read metaform://modules for the available capabilities, or search with different words.
prompts.triage_note: Results are trimmed to the fields most next steps need, so you read only those: view=full supplies full default detail while honoring explicit fields and filters, fields=[...] keeps the paths you name, view=count counts records by the named fields, and must_contain or status_equals filter lists before delivery. Meaningful false, zero and empty values remain evidence; missing and unknown remain distinct.
prompts.list_cut: more not shown, so you read only the records your decision needs: narrow the list with must_contain or status_equals.
prompts.compaction_state: Context compaction recorded, prior delivery markers cleared. Relevant instructions and node context become eligible again when needed. Current applicable tool instructions are required before execution. Metaform cannot establish what you retained.
prompts.compaction_open: The module is still open, so its tools stay listed to you.
prompts.guide_unkeyed: This call names no logical context. Read 's applicable instructions through its instruction URI or metaform_instructions tool=. Retain the returned session handle on subsequent calls so the receipt can be reused.
prompts.already_read: is unchanged from its delivery receipt in this context, so its body is omitted. Available continuation: . A receipt does not establish retained understanding.
prompts.module_index: Metaform is extended by named modules. Each module publishes its own capability description and commands. Read only the module you need for your work: metaform help <module> lists its commands.
